title: permanent_bipedal3 single-u64 fast path
description:
Implement `permanent_bipedal3` for $n \le 64$: the single-`u64`-pair fast path that uses `Bipedal3` arithmetic, walks `gray_code_iter`, and updates a single `Bipedal3` column-sum word in-place per step.

## Background

For $n \le 64$, the column-sum vector fits in a single `Bipedal3` (one `u64` pair). Each Gray-code step is then a single `Bipedal3::add` or `Bipedal3::sub` against the toggled column (also a single `Bipedal3`). The reduction at each step is `Bipedal3::fold_mul` (inherent on the value, paper Theorem 2.1).

This is the headline single-thread fast path. SIMD batching across multiple matrices (T12) and multi-word streaming for $n > 64$ (T14) extend this baseline; both consume `permanent_bipedal3` as the inner kernel.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_bipedal3(matrix: &Bipedal3Matrix) -> Fp<3>` exists, requires `matrix.cols() == matrix.rows()` and `matrix.cols() <= 64`.
- [ ] [hard] Implementation walks `gray_code_iter(n)`, updates a single `Bipedal3` column-sum in-place via `add`/`sub`, and folds via the bipedal multiplication tree.
- [ ] [hard] Output bit-identical to `permanent_ryser<Fp<3>>` (T7) on 1000 random matrices for each $n \in \{1, \ldots, 16\}$ and 100 random matrices for $n \in \{20, 24, 28, 32\}$.
- [ ] [hard] No `unsafe` (per the crate's `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`).
- [ ] [hard] `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` passes; large-$n$ correctness tests complete under 5 s each (the 32 case at ~$2^{32}$ ops fits the budget on the dev host without `--ignored`).

## Amendment 2026-05-10 (user-approved, Option A — trim large-n cross-check)

Criterion 3 originally required cross-checks at `n ∈ {20, 24, 28, 32}` × 100 matrices each. Computational reality (measured during T9 review on the dev host, AMD Ryzen 9 5900X):

| n  | per-matrix wall-clock vs `permanent_ryser` | 100-matrix budget |
|----|---------------------------------------------|--------------------|
| 20 | ~5 s (slow tier OK)                         | ~500 s             |
| 24 | ~80 s (slow tier OK)                        | ~8000 s (split needed) |
| 28 | ~1300 s                                     | infeasible         |
| 32 | ~2 hr                                       | ~8 days, infeasible |

Both `permanent_ryser` and `permanent_bipedal3` are O(n · 2^n); the bipedal path is O(50×) faster on the inner constant but n=32 still costs ~2 hours per matrix because of the 4.3·10^9 Gray-walk iterations. The 5 s/test default-tier and 120 s/test slow-tier limits cannot be met for n ≥ 28.

**Amended criterion 3:** Output bit-identical to `permanent_ryser<Fp<3>>` (T7) on 1000 random matrices for each $n ∈ \{1, ..., 16\}$ (default tier where each `n` fits the 5 s budget; slow tier for the rest) **and** 100 random matrices for $n ∈ \{20, 24\}$ (slow tier, `#[ignore = "sim: ..."]`). The original `n ∈ \{28, 32\}` cross-check at 100 matrices is dropped as computationally infeasible against any in-process Rust oracle on commodity hardware. Spot correctness at `n ∈ \{28, 32\}` is delegated to the SIMD batch path (T12) and the multi-word streaming kernel (T14), which use independent inner-loop strategies and therefore provide an algorithmic cross-check at those sizes once they land.

**Amended criterion 5:** the large-n cross-check tests live in the slow tier (`#[ignore = "sim: ..."]`); `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` (default tier) passes the n=1..16 default-tier subset under the 5 s/test limit. The original criterion-5 claim that "the 32 case at ~2^32 ops fits the budget on the dev host without --ignored" is contradicted by measurement and amended out.

Reason: epic criterion 2 (parent `ae82bd73` description) is amended in tandem with the same wording.
Approved by user 2026-05-10 (epic ae82bd73 session 3, AskUserQuestion option A).

## Amendment 2026-05-11 (user-approved, Option A — n bound + oracle for large-n cross-check)

Two surgical clarifications to align the criteria with `gray_code_iter`'s precondition and the slow-tier per-test budget. Both items were surfaced by the T9 rework-cycle-1 code review on 2026-05-10.

**Amended criterion 1:** `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_bipedal3(matrix: &Bipedal3Matrix) -> Fp<3>` exists, requires `matrix.cols() == matrix.rows()` and `matrix.cols() <= 63` (was `<= 64`). Reason: `gray_code_iter(n)` walks $2^n - 1$ transitions and is bounded by `1u64 << n` for the toggled-bit lookup; `1u64 << 64` is undefined behaviour in Rust. The single-word fast path is by definition bounded by what fits in a single `u64` of column-sum, and `n = 64` would require either a `u128` walk (out of scope; that's the multi-word streaming kernel T14's job) or a special-cased branch that does not compose with `gray_code_iter`. No known consumer demands `n = 64`; the SIMD batch path (T12) and multi-word kernel (T14) cover larger sizes.

**Amended criterion 3 (oracle for large-$n$ cross-check):** For $n \in \{1, \ldots, 16\}$ the oracle remains `permanent_ryser<Fp<3>>` (T7). For $n \in \{20, 24\}$ the cross-check may use `permanent_mod3_reference` (T8) as the oracle, via transitivity through T8's own bit-identical cross-check vs `permanent_ryser<Fp<3>>` at $n \le 12$ (12000 matrices, T8 criterion). T8 is the paper-faithful Julia port; it is `O(50\times)` slower than the bipedal fast path but `O(10\times)` faster than the generic `permanent_ryser<Fp<3>>` (which pays a trait-call cost per Gray step). Wall-clock at $n = 24$: `permanent_ryser` ~80 s/matrix (8000 s for 100 matrices, exceeds slow-tier per-test budget) vs `permanent_mod3_reference` ~8 s/matrix (~800 s, fits with per-$n$ test split). The transitivity argument: T8 ↔ T7 holds by T8 criterion's 12000-matrix bit-identical cross-check; T9 ↔ T8 at $n \in \{20, 24\}$ then implies T9 ↔ T7 at those sizes.

Approved by user 2026-05-11 (epic ae82bd73 session 4, AskUserQuestion option A on both questions).
